The spine is a separation the donor made but never stated as the point: a RUN is a property of the win rate alone -- the payoff never enters the calculation -- while a DRAWDOWN needs both p and b, because how far you fall depends on what the winners scattered through the fall give back. The expected WAITING TIME for a run, (1 - q^k) / (p * q^k), which turns 'will it happen' into 'how often': at a 45% win rate the first run of eight arrives every 263 trades, about fifteen months at four a week, so a decade of that system should contain about eight of them. And the percentage columns are computed by compounding rather than by multiplication: a 16R drawdown at 1% risk a trade is a fall of 14.8%, not 16%, and at 3% it is 38.1%, not 48%. WHY IT COSTS TO SHOW: a resting quote is a free option written to whoever takes it (Copeland and Galai 1983), and the quantity displayed is the size of that option. Hiding buys invisibility and pays in queue position, because display priority fills the shown part of every order before the hidden part of any of them; Bessembinder, Panayides and Venkataraman measured both halves on a market where the choice is explicit. WORKED EXAMPLE, TWO TABLES, ARITHMETIC VERIFIED IN PYTHON. A hundred tests of one level, display 200 every time. 58 traded under half, 22 traded over half without clearing, 6 cleared and price moved on, 14 cleared and refilled. The record bounds the true rate at 14% to 94% (the 80 blind tests could all have had it and none could have shown it) and estimates 70% only under an independence assumption the same data cannot check.
